edges.description: Mutant calsarcin-1 localises to the Z-disc and is accompanied by disrupted, misaligned Z-discs.
Interstitial fibrosis develops in mice expressing the human alleles. The intermediate steps between the allele and fibroblast activation are not characterised.

The originally proposed link, by analogy with the null allele: loss of calsarcin-1 function would release calcineurin. The HCM alleles themselves did not change calcineurin activity when expressed in mouse heart, so this edge is contested.

Proposed link: the abnormal Z-disc, rather than calcineurin or gross contractile failure, initiates the hypertrophic response. Inferred by the authors from the co-occurrence of Z-disc damage and hypertrophy with normal systolic function and unchanged calcineurin activity.
Myocyte hypertrophy is expressed at the organ level as increased septal thickness and left ventricular mass.
Myocyte hypertrophy with interstitial fibrosis and preserved systolic function together make up the HCM-like phenotype of the allele models.

Calcineurin-NFAT signalling is a hypertrophic pathway, and its release by loss of calsarcin-1 augments stress-induced myocyte growth. Shown for the null allele under pressure overload, not for the human HCM alleles.
Interstitial fibrosis is one component of the HCM-like phenotype of the allele models.
The model is the only source of evidence for this node.
edges.limitations: Transgene overexpression on a mouse background with sub-heterozygous mutant protein levels; no human tissue comparison exists.

nodes.description: Loss of calsarcin-1 releases calcineurin from inhibition, activates a hypertrophic gene programme without overt hypertrophy, and enhances the hypertrophic response to pressure overload; conversely, calsarcin-1 overexpression blunts angiotensin-II-induced hypertrophy. This is the gene's established physiological role. Whether it participates in human CMH16 is doubtful, because mice expressing the HCM alleles show no change in calcineurin activity. The node and its edges are kept, tagged with the alternative hypothesis group and carrying the contradicting evidence, to record that model; it is not wired directly to the clinical phenotypes.

nodes.description: Germline null mice lacking calsarcin-1. They have enhanced calcineurin signalling, an excess of slow skeletal muscle fibres, and a hypertrophic gene programme without baseline hypertrophy, and they show an exaggerated hypertrophic response to pressure overload. The model captures the gene's loss-of-function biology, not the human HCM alleles, which do not affect calcineurin activity when expressed in mouse heart.

Every reported MYOZ2 proband was ascertained through this diagnosis; carriers of the p.Leu169Gly allele without an accompanying MYH7 variant were clinically normal.

nodes.description: Interstitial collagen deposition, roughly doubling the collagen volume fraction, in mice expressing either human MYOZ2 HCM allele. No human MYOZ2 carrier has had myocardial fibrosis characterised by histology or late-gadolinium-enhancement imaging, so this is recorded as a model-derived mechanism node rather than a clinical phenotype of the entity.

nodes.description: Unexplained left ventricular wall thickening is the defining feature of the HCM series. The founding family showed pronounced cardiac hypertrophy with early onset of symptoms. Beyond that family, wall-thickness data exist only for single panel-detected carriers, too few to describe a MYOZ2-specific severity pattern.

evidence.reference_title: Myozenin 2 is a novel gene for human hypertrophic cardiomyopathy.
evidence.snippet: The phenotype was characterized by early onset of symptoms, pronounced cardiac hypertrophy, and cardiac arrhythmias.

nodes.description: The proposed initiating lesion is a heterozygous missense variant in MYOZ2, encoding calsarcin-1 (myozenin-2), a Z-disc protein that binds calcineurin and alpha-actinin. The founding alleles p.Ser48Pro and p.Ile246Met affect highly conserved residues. Only p.Ser48Pro has segregation evidence, and ClinGen scores the human genetic evidence as Disputed.

evidence.reference_title: Myozenin 2 is a novel gene for human hypertrophic cardiomyopathy.
evidence.snippet: Both mutations affect highly conserved amino acids. We conclude MYOZ2 is a novel causal gene for human HCM.

nodes.description: Cardiac-restricted transgenic mice expressing FLAG-tagged human wild-type or HCM-allele MYOZ2, including bigenic mice carrying the I246M transgene on a hemizygous endogenous Myoz2 background to approximate the human heterozygous genotype. The mutant lines develop mild myocyte and organ hypertrophy, interstitial fibrosis, Z-disc disruption and preserved systolic function, with calcineurin activity unchanged. Caveats: transgene protein was under half of total MYOZ2, residue 246 is valine rather than isoleucine in mouse, and only one S48P line expressed.

nodes.description: In mice expressing the I246M allele on a hemizygous endogenous background, about 14% of Z-discs are abnormal (poorly formed, interrupted, bulging or slipped, with myofibrillar disarray) compared with under 4% in wild-type transgenic controls. Phospho-ERK1/2 is higher than in wild-type transgenic mice, but the authors judge the data inadequate to name ERK activation as the driver of hypertrophy.
